memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Rejoice, you nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants; he will take vengeance on his enemies and make atonement for his land and people.'" — Deut 32:43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The song reaches its climax not in judgment, but in joy: "Rejoice, you nations, with his people... he will... make atonement for his land and people." After all the warnings, all the descriptions of judgment, the song ends on a note of hope and celebration. God will set things right, and — most wonderfully — He will "make atonement." He will provide the way for sin to be covered and His people to be restored. This is the goal toward which everything has been moving.

Notice who is called to rejoice: "you nations." This is not joy for Israel alone, but a summons for all peoples to celebrate God's saving work. From the very heart of the Old Testament, God's plan was always to bring salvation and joy to the whole world, not just one nation. His mercy was always meant to overflow to the ends of the earth.

This is so significant that Paul quotes this exact verse in Romans to show that God's plan always included the Gentiles — all of us — being brought in to rejoice with His people (Rom 15:10). If you are not of Israel and yet you belong to God today, this ancient song was singing about you.

And the word "atonement" is the golden thread that leads straight to the cross. The atonement the song promises is fulfilled in Jesus, who by His death made atonement for sin once for all (Heb 9:12). Because of Him, the nations can truly rejoice. So join the song. Rejoice with all God's people, for He has made atonement, and salvation has come to the world through Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I rejoice in the atonement God has provided in Christ?
2. How does it move me that God's plan always included bringing in the nations?
3. What would it look like to live with the joy this verse calls for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your song ends in joy and atonement. Thank You that Your plan always included me among the nations called to rejoice. I celebrate the atonement made by Christ, my Savior. Fill me with Your joy. Amen.
